title: A day-of-the-following-month term reaches QuickBooks as date-driven
custom_preconds:
Setup file (for Claude sessions; a tester does not need it)

Preconditions

  • Scenario: Your shop is connected to QuickBooks, and invoices a customer on a new day-of-the-following-month term of its own.
  • You are an Admin user working at {Location-A}.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • The test organization is connected to a QuickBooks Online sandbox company, and you can sign in to that company in another tab.
  • The shop's own term {Term-A}, due on day 10 of the following month, is not in QuickBooks. Customer {Customer-A} holds it and work orders {Work-order-1} and {Work-order-2} for it are complete.
    For example: {Term-A} is ZZAUTOTEST S8-02 Tenth, {Customer-A} is ZZAUTOTEST S8-02 Customer and the work orders are S2-15441 and S2-15442.
  • If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
custom_steps:
1. On {Work-order-1}'s Finance tab, set Invoice Date to Oct 5, 2026.
  2. Click Create Invoice.
  3. On {Work-order-2}'s Finance tab, set Invoice Date to Oct 28, 2026.
  4. Click Create Invoice.
  5. Wait until both invoices have synced to QuickBooks.
  6. In QuickBooks, open the Terms list (Settings, All lists, Terms).
  7. In QuickBooks, open each of the two invoices.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: the Due date reads Nov 10, 2026.
  • Step 2: the invoice is created.
  • Step 3: the Due date reads Nov 10, 2026.
  • Step 4: the invoice is created.
  • Step 5: neither invoice is on the QB Unexported report.
  • Step 6: {Term-A} exists as a date-driven term, due on day 10 of the following month.
  • Step 7: both read terms {Term-A} and due Nov 10, 2026, matching ShopView.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Credit terms", Confluence 963346440, version 3 (22 Oct 2026, "Renamed to Credit terms", Chris Ward), read 23 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11638, story SV-11677 (Story 8, QuickBooks sync - credit terms)

  • S8-R3: “A "Due day of the following month" term is created in QuickBooks as a date-driven term due on day X of the following month, so QuickBooks dates an invoice dated Oct 5 or Oct 28 with day 10 as due Nov 10, matching ShopView.”
  • S8-R1: “When a record is sent to QuickBooks with a term QuickBooks does not have, ShopView first creates the term in QuickBooks under the same name, then sends the record. This is how the standard terms already work today.”
